newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait students protest reported campus lesbianism.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait students protest reported campus lesbianism.

text.p: Some 500 Kuwait University students staged a sit-in strike on Wednesday to protest against a published report alleging lesbian activity on campus.

"We do not deny the existence of this phenomenon," said a member of the faculty of arts student union, Hanadi al-Otabei. "But we object to (Professor Alia) Shuaib for generalising and publishing it in a magazine sold abroad."

Shuaib has come under much attack by fellow professors and students since al-Hadath magazine quoted her in the November issue as saying that lesbianism was common among women in Kuwait, especially at Kuwait University.

University officials and students say the philosophy teacher has kept a low profile since the interview, but in a paid advertisement she has denied making the remarks, demanding an apology by al-Hadath to be published in all Kuwaiti dailies.
Al-Hadath's owner and editor-in-chief Madi al-Khamees told Reuters: "We have the tape and some of the stuff we did not use from Dr Shuaib is even worse than what has been published."
She was not available for comment.
Gay rights and sexual issues in general are taboo in the Moslem conservative Gulf Arab states, where clerics say lesbianism is against their faith.

The editor said the Information Ministry had referred him to the administrative prosecutor for offending the Kuwaiti public by publishing such claims, adding that his monthly received an official "final warning" of closure if it repeated the offence.
Some participants in Wednesday's strike said Shuaib should apologise and resign from Kuwait's only university.
